Krekenava Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Panevėžio apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Krekenava's Jewish community, settled in the early 18th century, reached 68 percent of the population by 1897. The town's main synagogue, built in the early 20th century, now serves as a sports center, marked by a plaque noting its original purpose; two smaller synagogues and a large Beit Midrash did not survive. On June 22, 1941, young Jewish men were arrested and shot outside town, and the remaining community was transported to the Pajuostė forest near Panevėžys on July 27, 1941, and murdered there alongside Jews from neighboring towns — roughly 200 people in total. This cemetery, partially preserved with about 30 surviving tombstones dating from 1863 to 1937, was being encroached upon by local farms when Lithuania regained independence in 1991, prompting its fencing that same year.
